 Stunning photos capture October's Hunter's Moon around the world 
 Image source, Tayfun Coskun / Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, A good view for the passengers of this plane flying over San Francisco Bay in California, US
 By Jo Wade BBC Weather Published 2 hours ago 
 The October full Moon lit up skies around the world this weekend. 
 Full Moons throughout the year have traditionally been given names that reflect what is going on in nature . 
 This particular full moon is known by several names, including the Hunter's Moon, a name rooted in historical traditions in the Northern Hemisphere. 
 The Hunter's Moon is known to sit in the sky for a particularly long time - similar to the preceding Harvest Moon - giving hunters extra light in the skies.
 Image source, BBC / BBC Weather Watcher Sam's House Image caption, The Hunter's Moon over Stoney Middleton in Derbyshire, UK 
 Image source, Gary Hershorn / Getty Images Image caption, An autumn glow as the Hunter's Moon rises behind the skyline of midtown Manhattan in New York City, US
 Image source, Davide Pischettola / NurPhoto via Getty Images Image caption, The Moon can take on an orange or reddish hue when it is low in the sky due to the scattering of short wavelength blue light as it passes through a large depth of the atmosphere, as shown here as it rises behind the Basilica of the Madonna dei Martiri in Molfetta, Italy
 Image source, BBC / BBC Weather Watcher Moxley Image caption, A view of the moon from Kimmeridge in Dorset, UK
 Image source, Salih Zeki Fazlioglu / Anadolu via Getty Images Image caption, The full moon glowing a beautiful burnt orange over the Galata Tower in Istanbul, Turkey
 Image source, BBC / BBC Weather Watcher Squiz Image caption, A clear view of the Moon in Felixstowe, Suffolk
 Image source, Ahmad al-Rubaye / AFP via Getty Images Image caption, Moonrise in Baghdad's Firdous Square, Iraq
